lesson.beat.adds.body1: Choir led Sam to the guitar. The guitar led to a band, and the band recorded a song. Luck lifted his path, and a hard year pushed it down. Some things were not his choice. Now let’s look at choices over just a few days.
lesson.beat.adds.heading: Choices add up.
lesson.beat.builds.alt: In seasons two and three, Path A’s skill bars rise faster than before, with arrows showing ball control helping passing and passing helping positioning. Path B’s bars rise slowly.
lesson.beat.builds.body1: Path A Maya stops staring at the ball. Now she can look up and see her teammates. So passing gets easier to learn.
lesson.beat.builds.body2: Each skill gives the next one a place to stand. Path B Maya is still working on the basics, so the gap grows.
lesson.beat.builds.closer.alt: Both skill boxes switch to basketball. Path A starts with part of Court sense and Passing already filled, carried across from soccer. Dribbling starts low for both. Path B starts low on all three.
lesson.beat.builds.closer.body1: At eleven, both Mayas try basketball. It’s a different ball, and dribbling with your hands is new.
lesson.beat.builds.closer.body2: But Path A Maya already knows where to stand and when to pass. That comes with her. Path B Maya has to learn most of it from the start.
lesson.beat.builds.closer.heading: Trying something new
lesson.beat.builds.heading: Then learning builds on learning.
lesson.beat.closed.alt: Rain clouds hang over the ridge. The lake trail beyond the bridge is marked closed. A ranger stands at the bridge.
lesson.beat.closed.body1: Last night, a storm washed part of the lake trail away. A ranger at the bridge says it’s closed. No plan can stop the rain.
lesson.beat.closed.heading: Something they couldn’t control.
lesson.beat.closed.option.ask: Ask the ranger about other trails
lesson.beat.closed.option.ask.feedback: The ranger smiles. “Have you seen the Waterfall Trail? It’s shorter, and it’s open.” It’s a lucky tip they never planned for.
lesson.beat.closed.option.home.feedback: Feeling disappointed is normal. Alfredo feels it too, and going home is allowed. But is there another good choice?
lesson.beat.closed.option.sneak.feedback: The sign is there because the trail isn’t safe. Sneaking past could turn a bad day into a dangerous one.
lesson.beat.cover.alt: A single dot marks the beginning of a life.
lesson.beat.cover.body1: Your choices shape where a life can go. Good and bad luck, which nobody chooses, shape it too.
lesson.beat.cover.body2: First we watch one whole life in half a minute. Then we go on a hike and meet a girl with two paths.
lesson.beat.cover.heading: The paths we make
lesson.beat.cover.lede: Your choices help pick the path. Good and bad luck, which nobody picks, change it too. The small things you do each day add up.
lesson.beat.explore.alt: This interactive map shows example life choices. At each fork, two or three choices branch ahead. Some close for a reason, and some lucky chances open. The chosen path turns dark green, with gray branches for choices not taken.
lesson.beat.explore.body1: Start at the beginning and pick a choice at each fork. Some doors close, and some open by surprise. You can always go back.
lesson.beat.explore.heading: Choose a life path.
lesson.beat.fork.alt: One path splits into two. On Path A, Maya keeps practising. On Path B, she mostly skips. After season one, Path A’s calendar is mostly filled, and Path B’s has a few practices. Both sets of skill bars are low, with Path A slightly ahead.
lesson.beat.fork.body1: Meet Maya. She’s eight, and she just joined a soccer team. Let’s imagine two ways her next three years could go. It’s the same Maya with the same start. Only her choices are different.
lesson.beat.fork.body2: In her first season, Path A Maya goes to most practices and kicks a ball against the wall at home. Path B Maya goes now and then. So far, the difference is small. Early practice often feels like nothing is happening. Something is.
lesson.beat.fork.heading: Same start, two paths.
lesson.beat.halfway.alt: The walkers climb to the big rock. Their water bottles are half full, and the lake is still far away.
lesson.beat.halfway.body1: Partway up, Alfredo checks his bottle. Half the water is gone already. The lake is still far away.
lesson.beat.halfway.heading: Half the water is gone.
lesson.beat.halfway.option.continue.feed: They’d reach the lake with almost no water for the long walk home. On a hot day, that’s dangerous. Dad says, “The lake isn’t going anywhere. Let’s turn back.”
lesson.beat.halfway.option.turn.feedback: That’s good thinking. The other half of the water is for getting home safely.
lesson.beat.life.alt: The map shows one life along a line of ages, from birth to age {end}. The path grows one fork at a time. At every fork, gray lines show the choices {name} didn’t make. Luck lifts the path, and setbacks push it down. Light green paths carry on past age {end}.
lesson.beat.life.altEnd: After the story, you can change one of {name}’s choices. A different life grows from that fork, and {name}’s own path stays on the map behind it.
lesson.beat.life.heading: One of many paths
lesson.beat.never-late.alt: Both Mayas practise basketball for a season. Path B’s calendar fills for the first time and her bars rise; Path A keeps her head start.
lesson.beat.never-late.body1: Path B Maya can start practising any season she likes. When she practises basketball at eleven, her skills grow too. She has more to catch up on, but the door is still open.
lesson.beat.never-late.body2: Real life is messier than this picture. Coaches, time and money matter. Luck does too. Sometimes luck is kind, and someone spots you and says, “Keep going.” Practice helps, but it doesn’t guarantee a result.
lesson.beat.never-late.heading: It’s never too late to start.
lesson.beat.plan.alt: A trail map shows the trail climbing from the trailhead through a forest, past a stream and up a ridge to Mirror Lake. Alfredo and his dad wait at the trailhead with full water bottles.
lesson.beat.plan.body1: Alfredo and his dad are getting ready for a big hike. They study the map. Then they pack snacks, jackets and a bottle of water each.
lesson.beat.plan.body2: Mirror Lake is a long way up. Nobody gets there in one jump. It’s one small step after another.
lesson.beat.plan.heading: Alfredo makes a plan.
lesson.beat.practice.alt: Alfredo and his dad stand at the trailhead. The backpack gains three cards, called Reading the map, Spotting landmarks and Resting before you’re tired.
lesson.beat.practice.body1: Over the next few weeks, they take short walks near home. Each walk starts from what Alfredo learned on the last one.
lesson.beat.practice.heading: Practice builds on practice.
lesson.beat.respond.alt: The walkers follow the open Waterfall Trail to a lookout beside a waterfall.
lesson.beat.respond.body1: They take the Waterfall Trail and eat lunch by the falls. Alfredo says it’s the best sandwich of his life. The lake can wait.
lesson.beat.respond.body2: That’s called resilience. You can’t control everything, but you can find a good way forward.
lesson.beat.respond.closer.body1: No, it doesn’t. Turning back, resting, asking for help or picking a new goal can all be good choices.
lesson.beat.respond.closer.body2: Alfredo can feel disappointed and still decide what to do next. Nobody has to pretend a setback feels good.
lesson.beat.respond.closer.heading: Does resilience mean never stopping?
lesson.beat.respond.heading: Plans change. You can respond.
lesson.beat.retry.alt: The walkers climb past the place where they turned back last time. They have plenty of water and reach the bridge over the stream.
lesson.beat.retry.body1: This time they carry more water and plan where to rest. Alfredo spots the big rock and the stream from the map.
lesson.beat.retry.body2: They aren’t starting from zero. Everything they learned comes with them.
lesson.beat.retry.heading: The second try.
lesson.beat.sort.alt: Six cards are sorted into two groups. Their choices are how much water to pack, turning back, practising with the map and asking the ranger. The storm and a friendly ranger being there were outside their control.
lesson.beat.sort.body1: Sort each card. Was it their choice, or something outside their control? Outside things can be bad luck or good luck.
lesson.beat.sort.heading: What was in their control?
lesson.beat.takeaways.alt: The life map comes back. It shows {name}’s whole path, and light green paths are still open past age {end}.
lesson.beat.takeaways.body1: Your choices matter. They’re just not the whole story. Lots of paths are still open. What will you practise next?
lesson.beat.takeaways.heading: What to take with you.
lesson.beat.turnback.alt: The walkers return to the trailhead. The backpack gains a new card, called Water for there and back.
lesson.beat.turnback.body1: They walk home without seeing the lake. Alfredo is disappointed. So is his dad.
lesson.beat.turnback.body2: But they learned something for next time. They’ll bring enough water to get there and back.
lesson.beat.turnback.heading: Turning back isn’t giving up.
lesson.practised.landmarks: Landmarks are things you see from far away, like a big rock.
lesson.practised.map: He finds where they are on the map, then picks the way.
lesson.practised.rest: They stop for a drink before their legs get heavy.
lesson.sort.ask: Asking the ranger about other trails
lesson.sort.done: They couldn’t choose the storm. They couldn’t choose a friendly ranger either. They could choose how to pack, when to turn back, what to practise and who to ask.
lesson.sort.progress: {count} of {total} sorted. Drag each card to a side, or tap Skip to see the answers.
lesson.sort.ranger: A friendly ranger at the bridge
lesson.takeaway.add.heading: Choices add up.
lesson.takeaway.add.text: Small things you do again and again can grow into something big, for better or worse. One hard day doesn’t decide your future.
lesson.takeaway.build.heading: Learning builds on learning.
lesson.takeaway.build.text: What you know gives the next thing a place to start. Sometimes that works even for something new.
lesson.takeaway.weather.heading: Not everything is yours to choose.
lesson.takeaway.weather.text: Some surprises are storms. Some are lucky breaks. Either way, you can pause, ask for help and choose your next step.

overview.description: Lesson 1: how small choices add up, why not everything is yours to choose, and how to keep going when plans change. A guided journey for ages 8+.
overview.heading: The paths we make
overview.lede: A life has more possible paths than anyone could walk. This lesson shows how the choices we repeat add up, how learning builds on learning, and how other people, help and luck shape the path too.
overview.title: Choices — The paths we make
overview.together.text1: Pause at the choices and ask what your reader would do. There are no wrong answers; the point is to notice what changes.
overview.together.text2: Use the ← and → keys to move through the story, or tap the chapters at the top to jump around.
overview.together.title: Reading together?

play.end.heading: Your summary

play.intro.text: Pick one thing each afternoon. Practice builds your skills, and rest helps them stick. Some days, things happen that you didn’t choose. Some of them are good surprises.

practice.beat.afternoons.body.new: A new box opens partly filled. Some of your soccer skills come with you.
practice.beat.afternoons.body.start: Pick one thing each afternoon. Your skills grow from what you pick.
practice.beat.afternoons.heading: Ten afternoons.
practice.beat.again.alt: Maya four times along one line of footprints: at practice, at practice in the rain, with her eyes on the ball, and kicking her ball against the wall at home.
practice.beat.again.body1: So she goes. The next week she goes again, even in the rain.
practice.beat.again.body2: At practice, she listens to the coach and tries hard. At home, she kicks her ball against the wall.
practice.beat.again.body3: Each of these is one small choice.
practice.beat.again.heading: Again and again.
practice.beat.basketball.alt: Maya at eleven with a basketball, under a hoop. Her basketball box: knowing where to stand and passing start partly filled with soccer’s stripes, and dribbling with hands is just starting.
practice.beat.basketball.body1: At eleven, Maya tries basketball. Some of what she built comes with her.
practice.beat.basketball.body2: She already knows where to stand and when to pass. Dribbling with her hands is new, so she starts that from the beginning.
practice.beat.basketball.heading: A new ball.
practice.beat.builds.alt: Three blocks like steps, each resting on the one before: Looking up, then Passing, then Knowing where to stand. Maya’s footprints climb them, and she stands on the top step.
practice.beat.builds.body1: Something else adds up too. Once Maya stops staring at the ball, she can look up.
practice.beat.builds.body2: Looking up helps her learn passing. Passing teaches her where to stand. Each skill gives the next one a place to start.
practice.beat.builds.heading: Skills on skills.
practice.beat.keep.alt: The map once more, with Maya’s soccer years drawn as the footprints they are.
practice.beat.keep.heading: Three ideas to keep.
practice.beat.late.alt: The map again. One path ahead turns green later in life and grows its own footprints: A later start. On the other paths ahead, a star marks A coach notices, and a diamond marks An injury.
practice.beat.late.body1: Anyone can start practising, at any age. Starting later can mean more to catch up on, but the door stays open.
practice.beat.late.body2: Real life is messier than this picture. Coaches, time and money matter. So does luck, good and bad. Practice helps, but it doesn’t guarantee a result.
practice.beat.late.heading: Never too late.
practice.beat.map.alt: Maya’s life on the map, from birth to today. A dark green line passes Starts school, Joins a soccer team and Tries basketball, with gray paths she didn’t take and light green paths ahead. A box marks her soccer years.
practice.beat.map.body1: Season after season, Maya keeps choosing practice. From far away, three years of it look like one long line.
practice.beat.map.heading: One season, then three.
practice.beat.maths.alt: Someone else’s trail of footprints, labelled Maths class, Homework, Homework again and A hard problem. It ends at a chalkboard: Mathematician.
practice.beat.maths.body1: The same goes for many things. Nobody becomes a mathematician just by deciding to.
practice.beat.maths.body2: A mathematician chooses maths class. They do the homework, then do it again the next night. Years of small choices like that are what a mathematician is made of.
practice.beat.maths.heading: Maths too.
practice.beat.next.alt: Maya dribbles her ball across the field and looks up, with her footprints behind her.
practice.beat.next.body1: What Maya practises gets easier over time.
practice.beat.next.body2: These days, she doesn’t think about her feet at all. So who is doing it?
practice.beat.next.heading: Coming next.
practice.beat.quiet.alt: Maya’s weeks of practice: season 1 is almost full, and seasons 2 and 3 are still empty. Beside them is her soccer box. Ball control is learning; passing and knowing where to stand are just starting.
practice.beat.quiet.body1: For a long time, it feels like nothing is happening. The ball still slips past her foot.
practice.beat.quiet.body2: Something is happening, though. Each practice leaves a little behind, even before she can see it.
practice.beat.quiet.heading: A long, quiet time.
practice.beat.steps.alt: The box on the map opens into a large view of the same stretch. Up close, the green line is a trail of footprints, labelled Practice, Practice again, Practice in the rain, Wall at home and Eyes on the ball.
practice.beat.steps.body1: Up close, the line is made of footprints. Each footprint is one small choice.
practice.beat.steps.body2: Most of them are the same choice, made again. No single step made Maya better. Together, they did.
practice.beat.steps.heading: Step by step.
practice.beat.want.alt: Maya stands with her ball at the start of a long path. Far along it, a small flag says Good at soccer. At her feet, an outlined footprint says Practice at four.
practice.beat.want.body1: Maya is eight, and she wants to be good at soccer. But she can’t choose to be good today.
practice.beat.want.body2: She can choose something smaller. Practice is at four o’clock, and she can go.
practice.beat.want.heading: Wanting and choosing.

reading.exploreIntro: In the interactive version, you pick one example choice at each fork, from age three to seventy. Here are some examples by age.
reading.exploreOutro: Some doors close for reasons you can’t control, like no places left, money or moving house. Others open by surprise. You can go back to any earlier choice.
